quote: A day so happy. / Fog lifted early, I worked in the garden. / Hummingbirds were stopping over honeysuckle flowers. / There was no thing on earth I wanted to possess.
source: Czesław Miłosz, Gift, lines 1 to 4, Berkeley 1971, The Collected Poems 1931 to 1987 (trans. the author, 1988)

evidence.where: Scottish Poetry Library text from New and Collected Poems 1931 to 2001 (Penguin, 2001, copyright 1988 onward), plus Poetry Chaikhana and A Year of Being Here, the latter stating the poem was translated from the Polish by Miłosz himself. All agree on the nine lines.
evidence.edition: The Collected Poems 1931 to 1987 (Ecco Press, 1988), the author's own translation; reprinted in New and Collected Poems 1931 to 2001

reason: The opening four lines of the nine-line poem match exactly across three reprints, and the self-translation credit is confirmed by a reprint citing the Ecco edition. The quotation stops at the poem's own full stop after possess.
